studies.title: Execution ownership and fault domains
studies.question: Which process owns work, and what shares its failure fate?
studies.intervention: At the same confirmed request boundary terminate the client or execution owner; retain a healthy companion in every arm.
required_observations: blind native-log reconstruction against independent ledger
studies.inference_rule: Surviving execution and collateral interruption, corroborated with process/source ownership, locate lifecycle and failure boundaries.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: Client independence trades against resident/shared-service cost. If client and owner are the same PID, report one boundary rather than inventing a distinct layer.
studies.alternative_explanations: Caller-owned execution versus independently service-owned execution; per-task fault isolation versus shared execution-owner failure.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions

studies.title: Public control integration and identity boundary
studies.question: How can another application control the platform, and whose identity/authority governs that control?
studies.intervention: Integrate one minimal supervisor through a public native entry, then repeat the same harmless operation with an unauthorized principal.
studies.inference_rule: Compare native and integrated permitted paths, then the reached unauthorized attempt; determine responsibilities the platform provides versus those moved to the integrator or OS.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: A local single-user interface is not presumed multi-tenant. Unsupported identity/remote surfaces remain capability entries; external wrappers must not manufacture product enforcement.
studies.alternative_explanations: Identity enforced at the native platform entry versus delegated to an integration wrapper or OS; public protocol integration versus core-coupled integration.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions

studies.title: Lifecycle cost and sharing
studies.question: What fixed and marginal costs arise from lifecycle and resource-sharing choices?
studies.intervention: On a matched calibrated host compare cold/warm invocation, then the same four tasks sequentially and concurrently; use one short fixed observation window chosen by pilot.
studies.inference_rule: Separate startup from task cost and compare identical total work at different concurrency; tie scaling/contending resources to actual ownership.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: Describe lifecycle tradeoffs and short-window contention. Do not infer sustained capacity, p99, leaks or long-run reliability. No arrival-rate sweep or soak test.
studies.alternative_explanations: Amortized resident-service startup and shared resources versus per-invocation process cost; useful sharing versus contention under identical total work.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions

studies.title: Context retention and information cost
studies.question: How does context maintenance trade information retention against model input cost?
studies.intervention: Use the same feasible long history containing protected constraints, a rule update and a completed-step receipt; vary only native compaction.
required_observations: all model calls and usage including compaction
studies.inference_rule: A retained constraint counts as integrated only if it reaches the next model request and supports the accepted task; account for summary-generation cost as well as reduced input.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: If no matched native control is available, report observational evidence only. Synthetic summaries establish plumbing, not semantic summarization quality. Conversation retention does not establish exactly-once external effects.
studies.alternative_explanations: Constraint-preserving context transformation adopted by the next request versus lossy transformation or ignored component output; net input savings versus cost transferred into summarization.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions

studies.title: Tool integration and authorization binding
studies.question: When a tool is extended, who owns schema, permissions and the binding from approval to dispatch?
studies.intervention: Implement one equivalent harmless operation through a public tool extension. Compare its permitted path with the native tool, deny it, and change the approved target through a supported public control.
studies.inference_rule: An extension is verified by actual invocation and authority behavior. A reached denied or changed-target attempt must be compared to the same extension’s allowed control.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: Public surfaces may differ; compare ownership and guarantees, not raw line counts. Unsupported target mutation is a capability result; do not modify core code to create the intervention.
studies.alternative_explanations: Native authorization preserved across tool extension versus an extension dispatch path that bypasses or broadens approved scope.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions

studies.title: Scheduling and failure diagnosis
studies.question: Where are tools scheduled, and can native traces explain the resulting latency and failure?
studies.intervention: Use the same four independent read operations. Prefer a public native serial/concurrent control; otherwise label sequential-model-dispatch as a protocol reference. Inject one reached tool failure in the batched arm.
required_observations: blind diagnosis with withheld fixture truth
studies.inference_rule: Use observed intervals plus native/source evidence to locate concurrency or serialization. Reconstruct the failed call and retry owner from native records before consulting fixture truth.
studies.limit_and_tradeoff: If the provider serializes calls, latency differences include model roundtrips and cannot be attributed wholly to the harness. Trace diagnosis reuses these runs; no separate fault matrix.
studies.alternative_explanations: Harness-concurrent dispatch versus producer-imposed or tool-service serialization; native causal trace versus disconnected events that cannot explain retry ownership.
completion_requirements: each arm has a classified terminal result or explicit blocked/unsupported/unobservable disposition; missing arms prohibit paired conclusions
